title: 21-Day Data Analyst Sprint
description: A 3-week sprint for someone with some basics to become interview-ready: SQL, data cleaning, two portfolio projects, Power BI, and interview practice.

weeks.focus: SQL fundamentals, data understanding, cleaning, EDA, and a first Power BI dashboard.
Advanced SQL, statistics, DAX, a second dashboard, and harder interview drills.
Case study, resume, behavioral stories, daily mocks, and applications.

days.goal: Understand how a data analyst works end to end and get your first dataset ready.
days.deliverable: Dataset downloaded, tables inventoried, and a Project 1 README started.

tasks.title: How a data analyst works end to end
tasks.details: Read the intro of Mode's SQL tutorial and learn the workflow: business question → data → cleaning → analysis → visual → recommendation. Install Power BI Desktop while you read.

tasks.title: Download and inventory the Olist dataset
tasks.details: Download the Brazilian E-Commerce dataset (free Kaggle account required). Unzip it, open each CSV, and record the row count, column count, and what one row represents.

tasks.title: Write the business context
tasks.details: In five sentences: who Olist is, what a row in the orders table represents, and one decision this data could inform. Send it to the coach for feedback.

tasks.title: Set up your project workspace
tasks.details: Create a GitHub repository named data-analyst-portfolio. Add a project-1-olist folder and a README containing your business context.

days.goal: Write working SQL against the Olist data and understand how joins change the answer.
days.deliverable: queries_day2.sql with 8 working queries.

tasks.title: SQL fundamentals
tasks.details: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, HAVING, and INNER/LEFT JOIN. Work through SQLBolt lessons 1–6.

tasks.title: Answer 8 business questions in SQL
tasks.details: Use DuckDB or DB Browser for SQLite. Queries: monthly order counts; top 10 categories by revenue; orders by state; average review score by category; delivery time trend; payment type split; top sellers; late-delivery rate.

tasks.title: Explain your joins
tasks.details: Explain INNER vs LEFT JOIN in your own words and show one query where choosing the wrong join would change the answer.

tasks.title: Save your query file
tasks.details: Create queries_day2.sql with all eight queries and a one-line comment above each explaining the business question.

days.goal: Profile every table and identify the quality traps before you analyze anything.
days.deliverable: Data dictionary, data-quality risk list, and a one-page understanding brief.

tasks.title: The data profiling checklist
tasks.details: Learn to check grain, keys, data types, missingness, duplicates, value ranges, cardinality, and time coverage before analysis.

tasks.title: Profile all nine tables
tasks.details: For each table: row count, column types, missing percentage, duplicates, and min/max dates. Build a data dictionary for orders, order_items, and customers.

tasks.title: Find the traps
tasks.details: List five data-quality risks, such as missing delivery dates or duplicate reviews, and explain how each could distort an insight.

tasks.title: Write the data understanding brief
tasks.details: One page covering what the data describes, its grain, the main quality risks, and five business questions worth answering.

days.goal: Clean the core tables with decisions you can defend in an interview.
days.deliverable: Cleaned dataset plus a cleaning log with before/after validations.

tasks.title: Cleaning decisions that survive review
tasks.details: Missing-data strategies, duplicate handling, type and date parsing, outlier flags, and referential integrity. Every change needs a reason and a validation.

tasks.title: Clean the core tables
tasks.details: Parse timestamps, handle missing delivery dates, deduplicate rows, validate keys across tables, and flag price or freight outliers. Keep the raw files untouched.

tasks.title: Validate before and after
tasks.details: Record row counts before and after cleaning, then run three checks: unique order IDs, valid foreign keys, and correct date ordering.

tasks.title: Write the cleaning log
tasks.details: Create a table of decision → reason → validation result. This is a portfolio artifact interviewers genuinely value.

days.goal: Turn charts into evidence-backed business insights.
days.deliverable: Six charts plus eight insight bullets.

tasks.title: EDA that produces insights, not charts
tasks.details: Use the workflow univariate → bivariate → time → segments. Write insights as observation → evidence → implication.

tasks.title: Analyze revenue, customers, and delivery
tasks.details: Explore revenue trend, average order value, top categories, regional differences, delivery performance, and review scores. Build six clear charts.

tasks.title: Write eight insight bullets
tasks.details: Each bullet must cite a number and end with why the business should care. Send them to the coach for critique.

tasks.title: Choose your dashboard story
tasks.details: Pick the three strongest insights and decide the one message your dashboard should prove.

days.goal: Get a working, reconciled first dashboard page.
days.deliverable: project1_v1.pbix with a working first page.

tasks.title: Power BI essentials
tasks.details: Import CSVs, build relationships, create card/bar/line/map visuals, add slicers, and write basic DAX: SUM, DIVIDE, DISTINCTCOUNT, CALCULATE.

tasks.title: Build dashboard page 1
tasks.details: KPIs: revenue, orders, average order value, on-time percentage. Visuals: revenue trend, top categories, regional map. Add date, state, and category slicers. Verify the model relationships.

tasks.title: Reconcile every number
tasks.details: Compare each KPI to a SQL query. Document any difference and fix it before moving on. Numbers that disagree destroy trust.

tasks.title: Capture what confused you
tasks.details: Screenshot the dashboard and note three confusing Power BI behaviors to ask the coach about tomorrow.

days.goal: Publish Project 1 and get your first honest interview score.
days.deliverable: Project 1 published plus first mock interview report.

tasks.title: Dashboard design basics
tasks.details: Action titles, visual hierarchy, clutter removal, consistent color, accessible labels, and one message per page.

tasks.title: Polish and package
tasks.details: Fix layout and labels, add an insight title, tooltips, and a data date stamp. Export a PNG screenshot for the README.

tasks.title: Mock interview #1
tasks.details: Ask the coach for a 30-minute mock covering SQL basics, behavioral questions, and a dashboard walkthrough. Score honestly and save the report.

tasks.title: Publish Project 1
tasks.details: README: problem, data, method, three insights, dashboard image, and tools. Push to GitHub and add the link to your portfolio index page.

days.goal: Master the window-function patterns that analyst interviews actually test.
days.deliverable: Eight advanced queries, a drill score, and a one-page pattern sheet.

tasks.title: Advanced SQL patterns
tasks.details: CTEs, subqueries, ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG/LEAD, and running totals. These are the patterns most analyst interviews test.

tasks.title: Write eight advanced queries
tasks.details: On Olist: month-over-month revenue growth with LAG, category rank per month, cumulative revenue, first and last order per customer, repeat-purchase rate, RFM basics, delivery SLA buckets, and seller ranking.

tasks.title: Timed SQL drill
tasks.details: Five questions in 25 minutes with no hints. Log every mistake with the correct pattern.

tasks.title: Build a pattern cheat sheet
tasks.details: One page of window-function templates you can reproduce from memory: ranking, running total, month-over-month, first/last value.

days.goal: Use statistics to judge whether a finding is real and worth acting on.
days.deliverable: Applied stats analysis plus a one-page cheat sheet.

tasks.title: Statistics that interviewers ask about
tasks.details: Descriptive statistics, distributions, standard deviation, correlation vs causation, sampling, confidence intervals, A/B test intuition, and p-values.

tasks.title: Apply stats to Olist
tasks.details: Examine the distribution of order values, the correlation between review score and delivery delay, and segment comparisons with confidence intervals.

tasks.title: Stats quiz and a causation story
tasks.details: Take the coach's quiz, then explain why one correlation you found is not causation and what evidence would be needed.

tasks.title: Write your stats cheat sheet
tasks.details: Define mean, median, standard deviation, confidence interval, and p-value in your own words with a business example for each.

days.goal: Define the HR business problem and the metrics before touching a dashboard.
days.deliverable: HR data brief plus metric definitions.

tasks.title: HR analytics context
tasks.details: Learn attrition, headcount, tenure, and the cost of turnover. Understand the questions HR leaders actually ask.

tasks.title: Profile the IBM HR dataset
tasks.details: Download the dataset, define the grain, build a data dictionary, calculate the baseline attrition rate, and list five quality issues such as constant columns or small groups.

tasks.title: Define five business questions
tasks.details: For each: the metric, the denominator, and the decision it informs. Bad denominators are a classic interview trap.

tasks.title: Write data brief v2
tasks.details: Repeat the Day 3 brief structure for HR. Note how the grain and quality issues differ from e-commerce.

days.goal: Find the real drivers of attrition without misleading denominators.
days.deliverable: Analysis queries plus six evidence-backed insights.

tasks.title: Metric guardrails
tasks.details: Denominators, small-sample groups, Simpson's paradox, and why attrition by gender can mislead without controlling for role.

tasks.title: Analyze attrition drivers
tasks.details: Attrition by department, role, tenure band, overtime, gender, and satisfaction. Use window functions for percentage of total.

tasks.title: Manual spot-checks
tasks.details: Verify three numbers by hand. Explain any segment with fewer than 30 employees that you decide not to highlight.

tasks.title: Write six insights
tasks.details: Observation → evidence → implication. Flag which findings are correlational and which need more data.

days.goal: Build an HR dashboard with measures you can explain under pressure.
days.deliverable: project2_v1.pbix with two pages.

tasks.title: DAX for real dashboards
tasks.details: CALCULATE, FILTER, ALL, DIVIDE, time intelligence, and measure vs calculated column. Focus on filter context.

tasks.title: Build the HR dashboard
tasks.details: Page 1: headcount, attrition percentage, department breakdown. Page 2: drivers — overtime, tenure, satisfaction. Add slicers and five measures.

tasks.title: Explain filter context
tasks.details: Pick three measures and explain what each calculates and how slicers change it. Verify totals against SQL.

tasks.title: Save DAX patterns
tasks.details: Note the five measures with their DAX and when to reuse each pattern.

days.goal: Make both dashboards answer a business question, not just display data.
days.deliverable: Polished dashboards plus fixes from mock feedback.

tasks.title: Dashboard storytelling
tasks.details: Audience, one message per page, action titles, annotation, color semantics, and executive summaries.

tasks.title: Revise both dashboards
tasks.details: Add action titles, annotations, and an executive summary page for Projects 1 and 2. Remove anything that does not support the message.

tasks.title: Mock interview #2
tasks.details: Ten-minute dashboard walkthrough plus one case question. Get scored on insight, structure, and design.

tasks.title: Apply the feedback
tasks.details: Fix the top three issues from the mock before moving on.

days.goal: Ship the second project and update your skill picture honestly.
days.deliverable: Project 2 published plus an updated skill self-assessment.

tasks.title: Portfolio READMEs that get interviews
tasks.details: Problem → data → method → insights → recommendation → what you would do next. Include images and links.

tasks.title: Publish Project 2
tasks.details: Finalize the README, add dashboard screenshots, push to GitHub, and add it to your portfolio index page.

tasks.title: Mock interview #3
tasks.details: SQL plus Python/pandas for 30 minutes. Review every missed question and update your skill levels.

tasks.title: Week 2 retrospective
tasks.details: Score your skills 1–5 again, list your three biggest gaps, and adjust next week's focus with the coach.

days.goal: Structure and present a business case in five minutes.
days.deliverable: One-page finance case plus a five-minute presentation.

tasks.title: Case interview structure
tasks.details: Clarify → structure → analyze → recommend. Practice stating assumptions out loud.

tasks.title: Finance mini case
tasks.details: Use the UCI Bank Marketing dataset. Define the campaign problem, clean the data, analyze conversion by segment, and write three recommendations.

tasks.title: Present the case in five minutes
tasks.details: Business problem, approach, three findings, recommendation. Get feedback on structure, not just the answer.

tasks.title: Write the one-page case
tasks.details: One page you can paste into your portfolio or discuss in an interview.

days.goal: Turn your work into a profile that gets callbacks.
days.deliverable: Resume v2, updated LinkedIn, and GitHub profile README.

tasks.title: The analyst resume
tasks.details: Impact bullets: action + method + result. Mirror keywords from job ads. Keep it one page and ATS-friendly.

tasks.title: Rewrite resume, LinkedIn, and GitHub
tasks.details: Add both projects with metrics. Update your headline, about section, skills, and GitHub profile README.

tasks.title: Resume critique
tasks.details: Paste three real job descriptions and your resume for the coach to critique against them.

tasks.title: Save target roles
tasks.details: Collect five to ten job descriptions you will actually apply to and note the recurring requirements.

days.goal: Build speed and accuracy under interview conditions.
days.deliverable: Drill scores plus an error log.

tasks.title: Interview SQL patterns
tasks.details: Aggregation, joins, deduplication, gaps and islands, ranking, and date math. Know the pandas equivalent of each.

tasks.title: Ten timed SQL and five pandas questions
tasks.details: 45 minutes total, no hints. Score yourself honestly.

tasks.title: Mock interview #4
tasks.details: SQL-heavy mock for 30 minutes. Think out loud and explain trade-offs.

tasks.title: Build an error log
tasks.details: Every mistake, the correct pattern, and the tell that would signal it next time.

days.goal: Have eight specific, metric-backed stories ready.
days.deliverable: Eight polished STAR stories.

tasks.title: STAR stories
tasks.details: Eight stories: conflict, failure, ambiguity, deadline, stakeholder, learning, impact, and teamwork. Each 60–90 seconds with a metric.

tasks.title: Write and rehearse eight stories
tasks.details: Draft each story, then say it out loud twice. Cut anything that does not set up the action or result.

tasks.title: HR mock interview #5
tasks.details: Behavioral interview scored on structure, clarity, ownership, and specificity.

tasks.title: Fix your two weakest stories
tasks.details: Rewrite them with a clearer stake, action, and measurable result.

days.goal: Perform under realistic pressure and find the remaining gaps.
days.deliverable: Panel scorecard plus a gap plan.

tasks.title: Panel interview strategy
tasks.details: Listen, structure, think aloud, handle unknowns, and ask good questions at the end.

tasks.title: Rehearse project walkthroughs
tasks.details: Two minutes each for Project 1, Project 2, and the finance case. Record yourself if you can.

tasks.title: Full panel mock #6
tasks.details: Technical, case, and behavioral questions for 45 minutes, scored across all competencies.

tasks.title: Gap plan
tasks.details: Identify the three lowest scores and schedule targeted practice before Day 20.

days.goal: Turn preparation into actual applications.
days.deliverable: 10–15 applications logged plus mock #7.

tasks.title: Applications that get read
tasks.details: Tailoring, cover-note templates, recruiter outreach, referral asks, and a simple application tracker.

tasks.title: Apply to 10–15 roles
tasks.details: Tailor your resume summary and two bullets per role. Log every application with date and follow-up.

tasks.title: Rapid-fire mock #7
tasks.details: 20 minutes of SQL and behavioral questions with short answers. Aim for clarity under pressure.

tasks.title: Update the tracker
tasks.details: Add follow-up dates and set reminders for five to seven days out.

days.goal: Measure your improvement and leave with a concrete job-search plan.
days.deliverable: Final report card plus a 30-day plan.

tasks.title: Negotiation and follow-up
tasks.details: How to discuss salary, ask for feedback after rejection, and follow up without nagging.

tasks.title: Final portfolio pass
tasks.details: Fix the top three issues a hiring manager would notice: broken links, unclear insights, or missing business context.

tasks.title: Final mock #8
tasks.details: Full panel. Compare your scorecard with Day 7 to see the improvement.

tasks.title: Write your 30-day plan
tasks.details: Applications per week, one weak skill to deepen, one new project idea, and how you will keep practicing.
